newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TNT to use Ansett money to lower debt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TNT to use Ansett money to lower debt.

text.p: World-wide Australian transport group TNT Ltd will use the money from the sale of its half share in Ansett Airlines to pay off debt in the short run.

TNT announced earlier this month the finalisation of plans to sell its stake in Ansett to Air New Zealand Ltd for A$325 million. The other 50 percent of Ansett is owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd.
TNT chief executive David Mortimier was asked in a television interview if TNT was going to use the money from the Ansett sale to pay off debt or for something else.

"In the first instance we need to reduce our debt further, which has been a burden for us particularly in Australia in the past 12 months and that of course will enable us, when the time is right and our earnings are much more steady, to be able to look at other opportunities for expansion," Mortimer said.
He was then asked if "the whole three hundred plus million" would go to paying off debt.
"In the short run, yes," he said.
TNT shares closed at A$1.56 on Friday, unchanged from Thursday.
